newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin presses for Russian membership of G7.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin presses for Russian membership of G7.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin pressed Russia's demands for full membership of the Group of Seven industrial countries on Wednesday, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said.

Kinkel said he had spoken to Yeltsin by telephone on the second day of a visit to Moscow and that the president had asked him about the prospects for a G7 summit which he has been invited to attend in the U.S. city of Denver in June.

"The president was especially interested in questions concerning the world economic summit and how Russia's full integration can be secured," Kinkel said after the 15-minute conversation with Yeltsin and separate meetings with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Defence Minister Igor Rodionov.
Asked if this meant Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin had asked for full membership of G7, he told reporters: "Yes, especially President Yeltsin."
Yeltsin has long asked the G7 to allow Russia into a fully-fledged Group of Eight, despite doubts by some of members that Russia was economically strong enough.

The G7 groups Germany, France, Japan, Canada, Britain, the United States and Italy. Kremlin leaders have attended annual G7 summits since 1991, taking part in political discussions but not being involved in economic matters.
